🇲🇽⚽ 4 YOUNG MEXICANS TO REPRESENT THE COUNTRY AT WORLD CUP OPENING

Four young women — from Veracruz, Iztapalapa, Gustavo A. Madero, and Oaxaca — will represent Mexico at the 2026 World Cup opening ceremony on June 11 at Estadio Ciudad de México, selected from over 1,000 video submissions.

Behind them: the Mundial Social program, which engaged 1.2 million young Mexicans across 96,000 teams from 28,000 schools.

Sheinbaum: "They represent their own effort, discipline, passion for sports, and love for what they do."

🔥🇲🇽 MARU CAMPOS HIDES BEHIND FUERO TO DODGE CIA INVESTIGATION

Chihuahua's governor refused to testify before the FGR despite a formal summons, invoking constitutional immunity to block the investigation into CIA agents operating on Mexican territory — allegedly with her government's approval.

She submitted a written statement expressing her "unwillingness" to provide information. FGR spokesperson Ulises Lara: constitutional immunity doesn't prevent officials from cooperating with investigators.

Morena's Ariadna Montiel: "This isn't political persecution. It's about clarifying serious facts that could undermine national sovereignty."

🇲🇽🇨🇺 SEMBRANDO VIDA EXPANDS TO 9 CUBAN PROVINCES — 15,000 PRODUCERS

Mexico presented the second phase of Sembrando Vida in Guantánamo, expanding the program from 2 provinces to 9 across Cuba plus the Isla de la Juventud. It will now reach 15,000 producers and 200,000 beneficiaries.

Phase one already boosted production and family incomes. Total investment: 588 million pesos — while Washington tightens the blockade, Mexico sends seeds and agronomists.

🇧🇷🔥 LULA: "WE ARE NOT A BARGAIN-BASEMENT COUNTRY"

Brazil's president fires at the US after Washington designated PCC and Comando Vermelho — Brazil's two largest criminal factions — as terrorist organizations.

"Don't play with the sovereignty of this country. Don't play with our democracy. We are not children," Lula said.

The timing: the designation came two days after Bolsonaro's son personally flew to Washington and asked Trump to do it. Brazil's Federal Police confirmed the groups "don't fit what the law classifies as terrorist organizations."

Inzunza to La Jornada)

AP/WAPO: "Mexico president Sheinbaum gifts her World Cup ticket to Indigenous athlete" May 29, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Sheinbaum gave ticket No. 00001 for the June 11 opener (Mexico vs South Africa) to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a 21-year-old Indigenous footballer from Veracruz. Three more amateur athletes got tickets for the Guadalajara, Monterrey, and CDMX matches. AP ran it straight, no editorial spin. 🇲🇽 Sheinbaum will watch the opener from the Zócalo Fan Fest with the public. • "I think a young woman who plays soccer is a great representative of our country" • "first female president in the country's 200-year history"

AP/WAPO: "Tomatoes become latest symbol of America's affordability squeeze" May 29, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Tomato prices up 40% — the biggest CPI jump of any food. AP names that Trump pulled the duty-free Mexican tomato deal and slapped on a 17% tariff, then attributes the spike to "a perfect storm of trade policy, extreme weather and Mideast policy." Quotes a NYC chef and three US academics. Zero Mexican growers. 🍅 Mexico supplies ~70% of US tomatoes; the 1996 Tomato Suspension Agreement survived five administrations before Trump killed it. • "A perfect storm of trade policy, extreme weather and Mideast policy" • "Tariffs are undeniably a big driver of the price inflation" • "The math is getting harder to ignore"

WSJ/DETROIT NEWS: Trump wants USMCA autos 82% North American, half US-made May 29, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Trump's USTR opens USMCA review demanding 50% of every car's value come from US factories — a unilateral rewrite of a rule the US itself negotiated in 2018. Coverage quotes zero Mexican or Canadian officials. 🇲🇽 Mexico's auto sector is the largest single exporter to the US; Ebrard called the 50% steel tariff at the same round "unsustainable." • "at least 50% made in the US" • "qualify for the trade pact's preferential tariff treatment" • "three to four years to be fully rolled out alongside elimination of products built in Canada and Mexico"

FOREIGN POLICY: "As USMCA Trade Talks Begin, U.S.-Mexico Ties Falter" May 29, 2026 | 🔴 📰 FP frames USMCA review as a Sheinbaum stress test — cartels, corruption, and tariffs bundled into one "boiling point." US "hawkishness" is presented as the weather, not a policy choice. 🔍 Mexico runs a ~$171B trade surplus with the US and supplies most of its auto parts; structural leverage runs both ways. • "Washington's increasing hawkishness... has pushed U.S.-Mexico ties to a boiling point" • "challenging political situation for President Sheinbaum" • "U.S.-Mexico relations could be derailed for years to come"
